title: Newcomer strategy, water reports and trail route approved
subtitle: Also covers Patricia Avenue stopping deferral, school bus zones, drinking water reports and active transportation crossings and bikeways.
overview: The committee recommended that Council approve Kitchener's first Municipal Newcomer Strategy, with $25,000 a year for Immigration Partnership Waterloo Region as an immediate action {{vote:m4}}. Other financial parts, including a newcomer internship pilot, go to future budget processes. Staff said most actions can proceed within existing funding and staffing.

On traffic and parking, the committee recommended a new school bus loading zone on Emerald Avenue, removal of the one on Prospect Avenue, and a parking ban on part of St. Leger Street {{vote:m1}}. A proposed weekday stopping ban on Patricia Avenue near J.F. Carmichael Public School was deferred to the June 29, 2026 Council meeting so staff can talk with residents, the school board and the parent council {{vote:m2}}.

The committee received the 2025 drinking water reports for information {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m5}}. It also recommended wayfinding, four trail crossings and neighbourhood bikeways for Active Transportation Route 2 between Stanley Park and Uptown Waterloo {{vote:m6}}. These are recommendations, and Council will make the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the first Municipal Newcomer Strategy, fund Immigration Partnership Waterloo Region at $25,000 a year, and refer other financial implications to future budgets.

decisions.item: School bus zones and parking changes
decisions.detail: The committee recommended removing the Prospect Avenue school bus loading zone, adding one on Emerald Avenue, and prohibiting parking on part of St. Leger Street, with the Uniform Traffic By-law amended.

The committee recommended deferring the proposed weekday stopping ban on Patricia Avenue to the June 29, 2026 Council meeting to allow engagement with residents, the school board and the parent council.
The committee recommended wayfinding for Route 2, pedestrian crossovers at four trail crossings, and neighbourhood bikeways on four streets, with the traffic by-law amended.
The committee received the report for information and directed that copies go to the Township of Woolwich and the City of Waterloo as regulations require.
The committee received the 2025 Drinking Water Quality Management System review summary for information.

debate: Councillors praised the newcomer strategy's engagement and said it should cover people new to Kitchener generally, not only recent immigrants. Staff said newcomers are defined as people here 10 years or less for engagement, while services are open to everyone.

One councillor was concerned about municipal finances and said support for the strategy did not commit to the budget items. Staff confirmed only the internship and contract staff actions depend on future budgets. Staff also said a calculation error in the internship cost had been corrected.

On Patricia Avenue, a councillor asked for a deferral because residents and the parent council were concerned. Staff said the school board raised the issue because buses were struggling to get through. Staff said they would look for another pick-up and drop-off area within a short walk of the school.

On water, councillors asked how regional and city roles divide, and staff said the Region supplies and treats water while the City distributes it and tests it. A councillor asked that regional salt and groundwater information be shared with the committee.

On Route 2, councillors asked about e-bike and scooter safety on trails, sign lighting, winter sidewalk clearing and phasing. Staff said a separate report would address e-bikes, the signs are reflective, and the capital cost is mostly trail paving.
